frame: Room 6's persuasive text is going to the council. The Stagglet ate the last page.
text: Build a Climbing Wall at Peaks Park! Every winter, Peaks Park sits empty, because there is nothing for young people to do there once the snow arrives. Our class believes the council should turn the old boat shed into an indoor climbing wall, and there are three strong reasons. Firstly, climbing builds strength, balance and confidence, and it is a sport that people of any size or age can enjoy. Doctors say that children who climb often sleep better and find it easier to concentrate at school. Unlike footy or netball, you don't need a whole team, so you can climb whenever you have a spare hour. Secondly, the nearest climbing gym is a two-hour bus ride away, which means most families on the island never get the chance to try it. A wall in the park would put the sport within walking distance of every school on Scaffold Peaks. Thirdly, a climbing wall would bring visitors to the park all year round, even in the middle of a blizzard. Those visitors would spend money in the local cafes and shops, which struggle every winter when the tourists stay away. The park's kiosk, which closes every June, could even stay open and hire local teenagers.
